A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StreamFormer research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original StreamFormer evaluations on THUMOS-14, YouTubeVIS-2019, VideoMME and MLVU, together with ablations and computational-cost measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds action-recognition comparisons, TVSeries, OVIS and StreamingBench results, and qualitative segmentation outputs.

M1.justification: The causal temporal attention, spatial LoRA, feature pooling and six-task training objective are retained. Renaming closed-set spatial pretraining from VIS to VOS does not change its pixel-classification procedure. Specifying LoRA rank and feature-extraction details adds documentation rather than a demonstrated method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds TVSeries online action detection, OVIS online instance segmentation and StreamingBench real-time visual-understanding evaluation. These substantially broaden evaluation coverage. K400 and SSv2 gain reported evaluation results but were already used for action-recognition pretraining; the relocated pretraining dataset inventory is unchanged.

E2.justification: New Table 9 evaluates against Toto and TRecViT; Toto was previously only cited. Table 11 adds comparisons involving InternVL-V2, Kangaroo, LongVA, VILA-1.5 and Video-CCAM, alongside Video-LLaMA2. Comparator membership in the original benchmark and ablation tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.3.2 replaces v1's explicit video-only segmentation training description with joint YouTubeVIS-2019/COCO training without COCO initialization. New evaluations specify TVSeries without flow, OVIS at 224p without COCO pretraining, and 16-frame StreamingBench evaluation. The substantive training-description revision does not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds qualitative online-segmentation sequences from the YouTubeVIS-2019 validation set in Figure 4. The pretraining-task, temporal-attention, data-efficiency and computational-cost analyses remain unchanged; the additional benchmark tables do not introduce new ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2 continues reporting point estimates without introducing a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Tables 9-11 report StreamFormer scores of 82.2/66.5 on K400/SSv2, 88.1 mAP on TVSeries, 20.8 AP on OVIS, and 58.24 overall on StreamingBench with category-level results. Figure 4 adds qualitative outputs. Original numerical table entries are retained; these additions are newly reported outcomes, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The causal mask, attention operations and training-loss mathematics retain their substance. Moving the text-encoding equation inline, renumbering equations, renaming VIS to VOS and correcting indexing notation introduce no substantive new definition, derivation, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a causal streaming backbone adapted from SigLIP, unified training across spatial and temporal granularities, and competitive, efficient downstream performance. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Supplementary Section 3.1 contextualizes the new causal-backbone comparison by emphasizing multitask breadth despite TRecViT's slightly higher SSv2 score. v2 also removes v1's computational-cost rationale for exclusively video-only segmentation training. Other interpretations and qualifications largely persist.

D1.justification: v2 specifies LoRA rank 32, identifies spatial outputs as last-layer hidden states, and identifies COCO pretraining inputs as VIS-style pseudo-videos. Most existing optimizer settings, hardware descriptions, VideoQA training details and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for TRecViT, StreamingBench, TVSeries, OVIS and several streaming or video-language approaches, while removing v1's two image-segmentation references. The related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain largely intact, with a limited additional discussion of causal-backbone comparisons.

P1.justification: Changes include localized copyediting, the VIS-to-VOS terminology correction, an acknowledgment, and expanded supplementary organization with pretraining-data and results sections. The main section order and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn to show annotation-to-feature alignment and a token legend. The pretraining dataset table moves from main-text Table 1 to supplementary Table 7, while Tables 9-11 and the multi-sequence qualitative Figure 4 substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The additional datasets and causal-backbone comparisons broaden empirical support beyond v1, while the redrawn framework and added implementation details improve clarity. The gain is limited by sparse protocols for new comparisons, differing StreamingBench frame budgets, and the unreconciled change to COCO joint training despite unchanged segmentation scores.
